Prevention: Avoid planting mango trees near alternate hosts like guava, citrus, melons, pawpaw, coffee, avocados and wild fruits to reduce pest population
Keep the orchard canopy open to improve aeration and spray penetration.
Harvest early when crop is mature and green because over-ripe fruits attract fruit flies
Lantana camara hedge rows to attract and host natural enemies like ants, rove beetles, birds and parasitic wasps
Release poultry in the orchard to feed on pupae at the base of plants.
Monitoring: Regularly check fruit surfaces for small holes, punctured fruit, black lesions, soft spots, rotting, maggots, discolouration and oozing sap.
Look for pupae 2-5 cm beneath the host plant.
Use fruit fly pheromone traps 1 trap per 5 trees to monitor presence of fruit fly (males)
Take action when 20 flies per trap are noticed.
Direct Control: The traps should contain ½ cup (150 ml) of vinegar mixed with water.
Trap fruit flies using pheromone traps - Methyl
Euginol (Bactrolure liquid) at 1 trap per 5 trees.
Till the orchard top soil (5 to 10cm deep) to expose pupae to the sun, birds, poultry and parasites.
Infested fallen fruits should be collected daily in a tightly sealed polythene bag and exposed to the sun for two days before burying (60cm deep).
Destroy fallen infested fruits to break the pest's lifecycle since pupation takes place in the soil.
Restrictions: When using a pesticide always wear personal protective equipment.
Follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage, timing of application, max number of sprays, restricted re-entry interval.
Always consult recent list of registered pesticides (PCPB).
Spot treat affected trees with poison baits of molasses with deltamethrin (Decis 2.5
EC) or bifenthrin (Brigade 25EC or defender 2.5% EC) or
DS) at a rate of 60ml per 20 litres of water every 5 days to two weeks depending on infestation severity.
U (unlikely to present acute hazard in normal use), PHI 8 hours.
